scenes.text: How to tell a *good burger* before you order

scenes.sub: Browning is flavor. A thin patty pressed hard on a hot griddle beats a thick, pale one.
Places that grind their own beef say so. About 20% fat is the target.
Soft, lightly toasted, just big enough. A bun twice the height of the patty is the most common mistake.
Bacon, two cheeses, onion rings and an egg isn't a better burger. It's a worse one that costs more.

scenes.text: First visit? *Order the plain cheeseburger.* It's the only way to judge the kitchen.
